# PPJ language reference

PPJ is OfficeKit's single public presentation authoring language. It is one
UTF-8 strict JSON file with schema `office-kit/ppj/v1`. Edit the file, then
use the CLI to validate, build, render and review it. JavaScript may generate
JSON externally, but JavaScript functions, JSON5, raw OOXML, XPath, relationship
IDs, network calls and executable expressions are not PPJ.

## Workflows

```text
new deck:       deck.ppj → check → build → render → review
third-party:    input.pptx → import → inspect/edit deck.ppj → build
OfficeKit PPTX: authored.pptx → import → exact embedded PPJ recovery
durable task:   add --task only when immutable revision/resume evidence is wanted
```

The CLI is `officekit ppj import|inspect|check|build|render|review`. Build
never overwrites the PPJ or its bound source. Render and review are explicit;
successful compilation is not visual approval.

## Root fields

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `schema` | yes | Fixed language identifier `office-kit/ppj/v1`. |
| `meta` | yes | Stable program identity, title, language and revision version. |
| `intent` | yes | Audience, brief, narrative, editorial constraints and delivery purpose. |
| `design` | yes | Canvas, theme, named styles, deck-specific Design Grammar and motion policy. |
| `assets` | no | Content-addressed local resources with rights and accessibility metadata. |
| `source` | no | Optional immutable third-party PPTX binding for source-preserving edits. |
| `components` | no | Finite reusable structures with parameters, slots, variants, repeat and simple conditions. |
| `pages` | yes | Ordered slides; each page's element array is the real back-to-front z-order. |
| `sections` | no | Persistent section membership over stable page IDs. |
| `customShows` | no | Named ordered page subsets. |
| `comments` | no | Persistent presentation comments supported by the language contract. |

All objects are closed: undeclared fields fail validation. IDs match
`^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:-]*$` and remain stable across edits. Coordinates and
sizes use points. Page order is `pages[]` order. Element order is back-to-front
`pages[].elements[]` order; do not invent a second z-index.

## Capability map

The language contains 1155 documented root/definition fields and
278 closed source-edit leaf kinds.
The following owners prevent a runtime feature from existing without an Agent
route:

| PPJ path | Owner | Surface | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `$.schema` | `language` | `ppj-state` | Fixed PPJ language identifier. |
| `$.meta` | `language` | `ppj-state` | Stable program identity and revision metadata. |
| `$.intent` | `authoring` | `ppj-state` | Audience, narrative, editorial and delivery intent. |
| `$.design` | `authored-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Canvas, theme, styles, design grammar and motion policy. |
| `$.assets` | `asset-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Content-addressed local media, rights and accessibility metadata. |
| `$.source` | `source-projector` | `native-ref` | Immutable third-party PPTX source binding and projection proof. |
| `$.components` | `component-expander` | `ppj-state` | Finite parameterized reuse with bounded repeat and conditions. |
| `$.pages` | `presentation-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Ordered pages, backgrounds, notes, motion and true element z-order, including capability-issued full-page or single-component sourceClone reuse and bounded topmost typed overlays. |
| `$.sections` | `presentation-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Persistent section membership. |
| `$.customShows` | `presentation-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Named ordered page subsets. |
| `$.comments` | `presentation-compiler` | `ppj-state` | Persistent presentation comments and replies. |

Simple text uses a string. Mixed formatting uses `paragraphs[]` and
`runs[]`; do not encode markup inside strings. Colors use theme references or
explicit typed color objects. Assets use relative URIs, exact MIME and SHA-256;
remote URLs and data-fetch instructions are invalid. Accessibility and rights
metadata travel with the asset or element.

### Native inline formulas

Use a formula run only when mathematical structure is part of the evidence.
Keep surrounding prose as ordinary text runs and omit `\(` / `\)`
delimiters:

```json
{
  "runs": [
    { "text": "Expected loss: " },
    {
      "id": "loss-equation",
      "formula": {
        "syntax": "latex",
        "source": "\\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i \\cdot L_i"
      },
      "style": { "size": 24, "color": "#172033" }
    }
  ]
}
```

This is a finite formula language, not TeX execution. It supports literals,
groups, subscript and superscript, `\frac`, square-root `\sqrt`, common
Greek letters and symbols, `\int` / `\sum` / `\prod`, roman text via
`\mathrm` / `\text` / `\operatorname`, common functions, bounded
spacing, and ordinary `\left` / `\right` delimiters. The source budget is
4,096 characters, 512 tokens, 32 nesting levels and 2,048 AST nodes.

Macros, environments, packages, conditionals, counters, I/O, matrices,
alignment, color commands and unknown commands fail before PPTX output. A
formula run may declare only `size` and solid `color`; it cannot carry a
hyperlink, font override, highlight, gradient, shadow or text decoration. The
compiler writes editable native `a14:m` / OMML, not SVG, PNG, a formula font
or literal backslash text.

Exact LaTeX recovery depends on the embedded PPJ snapshot. Importing an
ordinary third-party formula does not authorize OfficeKit to infer LaTeX from
OMML; the native graph remains preserved and unsupported edits fail closed.

### Element visibility and edit locks

Every typed element may declare `hidden` and `locked`. `hidden: true` keeps
the element and stable ID in PPJ but hides that object in the slide; it does not
hide the page or move the object in z-order. `locked: true` applies OfficeKit's
canonical edit lock for that object kind. It helps protect a finished visual
layer from accidental selection or movement, but it is not document security,
encryption, or an access-control boundary. Element array order remains the only
z-order.

Imported objects may change these fields only when their `nativeRef` issues
`setHidden` or `setLocked` for the current source revision. A partial or
extension-bearing native lock profile remains source-owned and does not become
an editable boolean.

## Preset geometry adjustments

`shape.geometry.adjustments` and preset `image.mask.adjustments` use one
complete ordered integer array. Omit it or use `[]` for the native preset
defaults. Percentage-like values use 100000 as 100%; angle values use 60000
units per degree. PPJ derives native guide names from the preset and never
exposes formula strings. The catalog contains 178
PPJ names; availability does not make a shape useful, so choose geometry by
information purpose rather than novelty.

Imported shapes receive `setGeometry` only when their native adjustment list
is empty/default or contains the complete canonical guide order with literal
`val N` formulas. Formula-valued, partial, reordered, duplicated, or unknown
guides remain source-owned and reject geometry edits. Canonical imported
picture masks use the same rule and receive `setImageMask` only for
`image.mask.adjustments`; preset identity and picture topology remain fixed.

## Authored compiler availability

Schema validity proves that a program belongs to the PPJ language; it does not
claim that every declared state already has a source-free native writer. The
compiler owns ordinary text, shapes with preset geometry and solid fills,
images and native image backgrounds, charts, tables, connectors, groups,
placeholders, notes, comments, sections, custom shows, transitions, animations
and Morph subject to the explicit boundaries below. A boundary fails before
writing output; imported native content remains source-preserved.

| Feature | PPJ path | Authored behavior | Imported/source-bound behavior | Current reason |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| bounded hierarchy display levels | `pages[].elements[].data.series[0].levels for treemap and sunburst charts` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the full hierarchy and exact display-level intent from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, only the generated visible shapes import as an editable group; omitted semantic descendants are never inferred from geometry. | Treemap supports 1..8 visible levels and sunburst supports 1..6 while validation retains the complete forest and parent totals. The compiler reflows visible rectangles or ring widths instead of deleting source data or reserving empty geometry. Other chart families, interactive drill-down and per-node visibility expressions fail closed. |
| editable mixed numeric Cartesian overlays | `pages[].elements[] where chartType is combo and one data.series[].chartType is scatter or bubble` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the exact numeric combo from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, axes and marks import truthfully as an editable group; arbitrary third-party shapes are never inferred as numeric chart data. | The bounded profile owns one shared value/value coordinate system, 2..8 scatter, bubble, line, area or column series and 2..64 strictly increasing finite X/Y points per series. It emits stable editable axes, fills, bars, segments and point marks. Secondary axes, chart formulas, statistical transforms, ChartPart build animation and unsupported styling fail closed. |
| bounded visible bubble sizing | `pages[].elements[].style.bubbleSizeScale and pages[].elements[].style.bubbleRadiusRange on bubble or numeric combo charts` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the exact size mapping from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, the generated ellipses and axes import truthfully as an editable group; third-party DrawingML groups are never inferred as bubble data. | PPJ can map one shared positive bubble-size domain through sqrt, linear or logarithmic scaling into a strictly increasing 2..72 point radius range. Declaring either field intentionally selects editable vector lowering because ChartML cannot promise exact visible radii or logarithmic transforms. Native ChartPart build animation, formulas, secondary axes, per-series ranges and reverse inference fail closed. |
| editable candlestick overlays | `pages[].elements[] where chartType is candlestick and data.series has aligned line, area or column overlays after the OHLC/HLC body` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the exact candlestick and overlay semantics from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, the generated price and overlay marks import truthfully as an editable group; arbitrary third-party groups are not inferred as financial charts. | The first series remains the bounded OHLC/HLC body and up to four aligned overlays may add line, area or column evidence on the same scale. Filled overlays render behind wicks and bodies while line overlays render above them. Numeric X channels, secondary axes, formulas and unsupported overlay topology fail closed. |
| editable pictographic bars | `pages[].elements[] where chartType is bar or column and data.series[0].symbol is present` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the exact pictographic chart from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, repeated units import truthfully as an editable group; arbitrary third-party shapes are never inferred as chart data and receive no pictographic mutation capability. | The compiler expands one bounded series into stable editable named-icon or preset-geometry units. It requires 2..12 categories, exact positive unit divisibility, at most 32 units per category and 192 total. Fractional symbols, multiple series, axes, ChartPart build animation and unsupported series options fail closed. |
| editable streamgraph | `pages[].elements[] where chartType is area and style.stacking is stream` | `partial` | OfficeKit-authored PPTX restores the exact streamgraph from its embedded PPJ program. Without that private program, the generated DrawingML imports truthfully as an editable group; arbitrary third-party paths are never inferred as stream semantics and receive no stream mutation capability. | The compiler owns a bounded centered silhouette with 2..12 complete non-negative series over 3..64 ordered categories. It emits stable editable cubic paths and labels. Native ChartParts have no centered-stream stacking mode, so ChartPart build animation, negative or missing values, secondary axes, per-point labels and unsupported series options fail closed. |

Each capability owns only its declared field group and patches the existing ChartPart. | PPJ owns plot-, series- and sparse point-level label visibility, common plot enums/integers/booleans, native position, direct number format and bounded typography; bubble scale from 0 through 300; native area/width size semantics; presence-aware axis reversal, finite numeric bounds/units and tick intervals; and direct RGB/no-fill axis and major-grid lines. Exact visible radii and logarithmic sizing are a separate authored vector capability, not a native source-bound ChartPart mutation. The source-bound run profile accepts only a direct soft edge, outer-shadow→soft-edge or full-span reflection→soft-edge, preserves the preceding owner proof and token-splices the selected run radius; the defaultText profile proves direct a:p/a:pPr/a:defRPr ownership and token-splices its softEdge/@rad, as covered by PpjSourceBoundTextSoftEdgeEditsDirectRunOwnerAndReprojects and its focused default-text extension. 3-D, WordArt and arbitrary effect lists remain outside this authored owner. |

| structured chart titles and other chart typography | `chart.title, chart.style.titleTextStyle, chart.style.legendTextStyle, chart.style.dataLabels.textStyle and chart axes textStyle/titleTextStyle` | `partial` | Bounded multi-paragraph/run chart titles are projected and editable through setChartTitle; canonical legend, data-label, axis-title and axis tick-label typography remains editable through setChartTextStyle. Unsupported title containers remain source-preserved. | Authored ordinary and combo charts own structured title runs plus Latin/East Asian typefaces, size, bold, italic and direct RGB/alpha. Formula-backed titles, hyperlinks, theme transforms, WordArt, shadows, effects and unknown title topology remain outside the bounded profile. |
| third-party media playback graphs | `pages[].elements[] where type is media and nativeRef is present` | `source-bound-only` | Imported audio/video pictures, media relationships and timing graphs remain opaque-preserved unless a future capability proves the complete playback closure. | Source-free PPJ owns a bounded canonical audio/video profile with an explicit poster, trim, loop and mute. It does not claim arbitrary third-party triggers, bookmarks, media effects or timing topology. |
| third-party partial element lock profiles | `pages[].elements[].locked` | `partial` | A recognized unlocked baseline or complete OfficeKit lock profile issues setLocked. Partial flags, extension-bearing locks and unknown combinations remain source-owned. Element visibility is proven separately and may still issue setHidden. | One PPJ boolean cannot preserve the intent of every type-specific DrawingML lock combination without erasing native information. |
| source-free OLE | `pages[].elements[] where type is ole` | `source-bound-only` | Imported OLE objects are classified and preserved; only issued nativeRef or typed capabilities may change them. | PPJ models OLE persistent state, but authored native OLE creation is not compiler-owned. |
| native Office SmartArt parts | `pages[].elements[] where type is smartArt` | `partial` | Authored PPJ emits one native diagram frame with data, layout, style, colors and cached-drawing parts. Custom definition assets execute bounded placement, gap, column and reverse operators and round-trip as content-addressed JSON. OfficeKit-owned native graphs issue text, connection, frame and verified detach capabilities; a picture-layout graph whose cached drawing has one embedded blip per node additionally projects canonical stretch/tile crop/opacity paint and issues setSmartArtImage/setSmartArtImagePaint for replacing an existing content-addressed node asset or its cached paint. Every closed third-party diagram projects as typed SmartArt: proven nodes and parent edges are editable by issued text leaves, while unknown graphs stay typed read-only with path-independent section hashes. | Arbitrary DiagramML programs, unsupported operator kinds, shared or external native closures, multiple/effect-bearing/linked picture blips and unverified caches fail closed. Picture asset/image add/remove and topology edits are not exposed. detachToShapes is explicit and reports semantic loss. |
| native-theme bullet identity and uncommon numbering schemes | `text.paragraphs[].style.bullet` | `partial` | Existing paragraph bullet leaves are editable only when capability-issued. | Authored bullets accept literal RGB/alpha or deck-local color tokens resolved to RGB/alpha, plus the documented decimal, alpha and Roman schemes. Existing native theme-token identity remains source-bound and leaf-editable rather than being guessed during source-free authoring. |

## Components terminate

Components have a finite frame, typed parameters, named slots, explicit
variants, bounded repeat items and only `equals`, `notEquals`, `present`
or `absent` conditions. They cannot call themselves recursively. Expanded
IDs are deterministic. A component is reuse, not a hidden script.

## Imported PPTX and nativeRef

Import copies the source package into a content-addressed local asset and binds
its SHA-256. Every visible object becomes a typed element or `opaque` with a
`nativeRef`. A nativeRef lists only capability-issued fields. Edit those
fields and keep its expected revision/hash; unsupported topology stays opaque.
No-op build returns the source bytes exactly. A stale, ambiguous or undeclared
mutation fails instead of rebuilding or flattening the source.

### Imported presentation canvas

An imported `design.canvas` is editable only when its own `nativeRef` issues
`setCanvas` for `canvas.width` and `canvas.height`. Values stay in points.
Keep the nativeRef unchanged, edit one or both dimensions, then build and
re-import. The compiler changes only the native presentation canvas: it never
scales, reflows, crops or moves slide, layout, master or element coordinates.
Because every page is composed against that canvas, render and review every
page for exposed margins, clipping and changed balance after the edit.

### Imported raster/SVG fallback pairs

PowerPoint may store one visible picture as a raster compatibility fallback
plus an SVG used by modern hosts. PPJ projects these as two local assets:

- `image.asset` is the raster fallback;
- `image.svgAsset` is the true SVG member.

Change `svgAsset` only when that image's `nativeRef` issues `replaceSvg` for
`image.svgAsset`. Declare the replacement as a new content-addressed local
`image/svg+xml` asset, keep `asset`, the image ID and nativeRef unchanged,
then build and re-import. PPJ cannot add or remove the pair and does not invent
a raster fallback. Review the modern SVG render; when an older host matters,
record separately that its unchanged raster fallback may still show the prior
artwork.

### Closed imported leaf vocabulary

The compiler may issue the following bounded leaves after importing the exact

`typed-operation` values are expressed by the typed PPJ element field named

An imported native leaf has a stable opaque ID, a closed kind, the expected
source-value hash and its current scalar value. Change only `value`; never
invent an ID, kind or hash:

```json
{
  "nativeRef": {
    "handle": "nr-…",
    "sourceSha256": "<64 lowercase hex>",
    "revision": "pptx-…",
    "objectHash": "<64 lowercase hex>",
    "capabilitySetSha256": "<64 lowercase hex>",
    "capabilities": [],
    "leaves": [
      {
        "id": "leaf-font-size-…",
        "kind": "fontSizePoints",
        "expectedHash": "<64 lowercase hex>",
        "value": 18
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

For an imported deck, change `pages[]` order only when every moved page's
`nativeRef` advertises `reorder` with `pageOrder`. The projected page ID is
anchored to its source SlidePart, and unchanged page-local element IDs survive
the move. This is distinct from element `reorder/zOrder`, which changes the
stack inside one page. Do not combine page deletion and reorder in one build.
If modeled `sections[]` exist, update their `pages` arrays in the same program
so they still form one complete partition in the new presentation order.
Comments and custom shows keep referring to the same stable page IDs. An
opaque section graph receives no page-order capability and remains unchanged.

To reuse one complete imported page, find a page whose `nativeRef` advertises
`duplicate` with `pageClone`. Insert one fresh page immediately after that
source page with an empty `elements` array and
`sourceClone: { page: "<source-page-id>", capability: "<issued-capability-id>" }`.
Do not copy nativeRef, element state, layout, background, notes, transition,
animation or visibility into the pending clone. Build and re-import first; the
new SlidePart then projects as an ordinary source-bound page whose full typed
or opaque content can be inspected and edited through its newly issued
capabilities. One source page may have only one pending clone, and the same
build cannot also delete/reorder pages or change section/custom-show routes.

To reuse one exact top-level component instead of the full page, add
`retainElement: "<source-element-id>"` to that same `sourceClone`. The ID
must name one direct entry in the source page's `elements[]`; keep the owning
top-level group when the desired object is nested. Every omitted sibling must
freshly advertise `delete` with `element`. The compiler retains the selected
native graph unchanged and lowers all sibling removals through the existing
deletion proofs. The pending page stays empty until build and re-import, when
the retained component becomes an ordinary source-bound typed or opaque node
with fresh nativeRef capabilities. This is not arbitrary graph extraction and
does not port the JavaScript repeated-candidate workflow into PPJ.

To continue an ordinary imported page without cloning it, require the page's
`nativeRef` to advertise `appendElement` with `elements`. Keep every
source-projected element unchanged and in its original order, then append new
typed elements at the end of `pages[].elements[]`. This suffix is above all
source-owned objects. The bounded profile accepts `text`, `image`, and
`shape` only when the shape preset is `rect`, `roundRect`, or `ellipse`;
the text type lowers to the native textbox profile. New elements have fresh
IDs and no nativeRef. Do not interleave them with native elements, add a paired
SVG fallback, or combine the append with another source mutation. Build and
re-import before the next edit so the new native objects receive fresh stable
source-bound IDs and capability evidence.

For imported object motion, change the complete `pages[].animations[]` array
only when that page's `nativeRef` advertises `setAnimations` with
`animations`. The capability is issued only for an absent safely addable
timing graph or an existing canonical editable graph, and never for a Morph
page. Targets remain stable PPJ element IDs; the compiler privately resolves
their current native bindings, including supported group descendants. Opaque
third-party timing receives no capability and remains byte-preserved. Build
and re-import a newly appended overlay before using it as an animation target.
Structural round-trip is not desktop playback evidence.

OfficeKit-authored PPTX embeds canonical PPJ and a node map. Import restores
that PPJ exactly when valid. If native software changed the PPTX but left the
embedded program, PPJ remains authoritative; a future build writes a new output
and never overwrites the input.

## Hard budgets

| Budget | Limit |
| --- | ---: |
| PPJ UTF-8 bytes | 16777216 |
| pages | 512 |
| expanded elements | 100000 |
| one repeat | 1024 |
| component expansion depth | 16 |

Budget, reference, type, cycle and source-capability errors are reported before
compilation. `ppj check --fix` may normalize deterministic formatting; it
must not choose layout, rewrite copy or change design semantics.

## Capability ownership

| Class | Current entries | Meaning |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `ppj-state` | 66 | Persistent authored state represented directly by office-kit/ppj/v1. |
| `native-ref` | 37 | Imported-source capability represented by opaque/nativeRef and lowered fail-closed by C#. |
| `compiler-helper` | 29 | Legacy facade or convenience constructor; not a public PPJ 2.0 authoring primitive. |
| `inspect-review` | 19 | Discovery, validation, rendering, review, or package interoperability rather than persistent deck state. |
| `host-only` | 13 | Operation against an open desktop PowerPoint session; never serialized into PPJ. |

The registry classifies legacy facade APIs while PPJ 2.0 converges. A
`compiler-helper` is not Agent syntax. PowerPoint Live operations remain in
the separate host-only list and never serialize into PPJ.

## Common mistakes

- Editing a PPTX package path instead of its PPJ ID or issued nativeRef.
- Reordering a type-specific collection instead of the page element array.
- Putting base64, HTTP URLs, functions or expressions in the program.
- Treating opaque-preserved as editable, or rebuilding the whole deck after a
  rejected source-bound edit.
- Calling build success a render, visual review or PowerPoint playback result.
- Using components as an unbounded layout engine instead of explicit finite
  reuse.
